outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to Efficient Adaptation of Foundation Models
outline.description: This chapter sets the stage by discussing the ubiquity of large foundation models (LLMs, Vision Transformers, Diffusion Models) and the prohibitive cost of training them from scratch. It introduces the critical challenge of adapting these massive models to downstream tasks and reviews the landscape of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) methods, including Full Fine-tuning, Adapter Tuning, Prompt Tuning, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), and Orthogonal Fine-Tuning (OFT). The chapter concludes by identifying the specific limitations of current OFT methods—specifically their high parameter count when attempting to maintain dense connectivity—and outlines the motivation for developing a more efficient solution.
subtopics: The Rise of Large Foundation Models and Training Costs
Deep Dive into Model Fine-tuning vs. Adapters vs. Prompts
Principles of Orthogonal Fine-Tuning (OFT): Preserving Pairwise Angles
Limitations of Block-Diagonal Structures in Current OFT Methods
The Problem Statement: Balancing Expressivity, Regularity, and Parameter Efficiency

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: An Information Transmission Framework for Matrix Factorization
outline.description: This chapter introduces a novel theoretical perspective for analyzing parameter efficiency in fine-tuning: viewing matrix operations as information transmission problems. It breaks down the mechanics of generating a dense orthogonal matrix through the multiplication of sparse matrices. Students will learn how to visualize matrix factorization as a grid-structured graph where nodes represent dimensions and edges represent information flow. The chapter establishes the 'desiderata' for an ideal factorization: dense connectivity (every node reaches every other node) and minimum free edges (maximum parameter efficiency under orthogonality constraints).
subtopics: Preliminaries: Reparameterizing Weights with Orthogonal Matrices
The Information Transmission Analogy: Grid Graphs and Connectivity
Visualizing Sparsity Patterns as Directed Edges Between Levels
Desiderata for Efficient Factorization: Dense Connectivity vs. Minimum Edges
Constraints Imposed by Orthogonality on Graph Topologies
Why Naive Dense Connections Fail Parameter Efficiency Goals

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: The Butterfly Structure and Orthogonal Butterfly (BOFT)
outline.description: Building on the information transmission framework, this chapter details the core innovation of the paper: Orthogonal Butterfly (BOFT). It draws parallels between the proposed method and the Cooley-Tukey Fast Fourier Transform algorithm. The chapter defines 'butterfly factors,' recursive butterfly matrices, and block-butterfly components mathematically. It explains how these structures allow for the construction of a dense orthogonal matrix using only O(d log d) parameters instead of O(d^2). Furthermore, it covers practical implementation details such as Identity Initialization strategies and a novel 'Multiplicative Dropout' technique designed specifically for multiplicative weight updates.
